title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of: I. vehicles with regard to the limitation of their maximum speed or their adjustable speed limitation function; II. vehicles with regard to the installation of a speed limitation device (SLD) or adjustable speed limitation device (ASLD) of an approved type; III. speed limitation devices (SLD) and adjustable speed limitation devices (ASLD)
scope_summary: UN R89 covers three approvals. Part I approves vehicles with regard to speed limitation (SLD/SLF or ASLD/ASLF). Part II approves the installation of separately approved SLDs/ASLDs. Part III approves SLDs and ASLDs as separate devices. The mandatory-type speed limitation (SLD/SLF) concerns vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3, while the driver-adjustable limitation (ASLD/ASLF) concerns all M and N vehicles when fitted.
scope_quote: 1.1.1 Part I: Vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3 equipped with an SLD and to vehicles of categories M and N equipped with an adjustable speed limitation device ASLD which have not been separately approved according to Part III of this Regulation, or to vehicles so designed and/or equipped that their component parts can be regarded as totally or partially fulfilling the function of an SLD or ASLD, as appropriate. 1.1.2 Part II: The installation on vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3 of SLDs and installation on vehicles of categories M and N of ASLD which have been type approved to Part III of this Regulation. 1.1.3 Part III: SLDs which are intended to be fitted to vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3 and ASLD which are intended to be fitted to vehicles of categories M and N. 1.2 Purpose The purpose of this Regulation is to limit the road speed of vehicles by means of a vehicle system which has the primary function of controlling the fuel feed to the engine or via the engine management.
applies_to_components: vehicle parts related to speed limitation (fuel feed control / engine management)
speed limiter plate in driving compartment ("SPEED LIMITER FITTED")
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3) (TRANS/SC1/WP29/78 and Amend.1)
Part II covers installation on vehicles of SLDs/ASLDs type-approved to Part III of this same Regulation; Part I covers vehicles whose SLD/ASLD has not been separately approved under Part III
Approval mark may be combined with marks of other UN Regulations annexed to the 1958 Agreement (para. 4.5)
Recommended to apply the SLD provisions to vehicles over 10 tonnes for which the limitation speed is less than the general speed limitation (footnote 2)

defined_terms.label: V
defined_terms.definition: The maximum speed of the vehicle such that its design or equipment does not permit a response after a positive action on the accelerator control.

defined_terms.label: Vset
defined_terms.definition: The intended mean vehicle speed when operating in a stabilized condition.

defined_terms.label: Vstab
defined_terms.definition: The mean vehicle speed specified in para. 1.1.4.2.3.3 of Annex 5 and para. 1.5.4.1.2.3 of Annex 6.

defined_terms.label: Vmax
defined_terms.definition: The maximum speed reached by the vehicle in the first half period of the response curve as defined in Annex 5 (para. 1.1.4.2.4).

defined_terms.label: Vadj
defined_terms.definition: The speed voluntarily set by the driver.

defined_terms.label: ASLF
defined_terms.definition: A function which allows the driver to set a vehicle speed Vadj and, when activated, limits the vehicle automatically to that speed.

defined_terms.label: SLF
defined_terms.definition: A function to control the fuel feed of the vehicle or engine management in order to limit the vehicle speed to a fixed maximum value.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles which do not differ in essential respects such as make and type of SLD, range of settable limitation speeds, ratio of maximum engine power/unladen mass and highest ratio of engine speed/vehicle speed in top gear.

defined_terms.label: Unladen mass
defined_terms.definition: The mass of the vehicle in running order without crew, passengers or load, but with full fuel tank, usual tools and spare wheel where applicable.

defined_terms.label: SLD
defined_terms.definition: A device whose primary function is to control the fuel feed to the engine in order to limit the vehicle speed to the specified value.

defined_terms.label: ASLD
defined_terms.definition: A device (not separately defined in para. 2) that, when fitted, limits the speed of M and N vehicles to a speed voluntarily set by the driver when activated.

defined_terms.label: SLD type
defined_terms.definition: SLDs which do not differ in essential characteristics such as make and type, the range of settable speed values and the method used to control the engine fuel feed.

applicability_hints: Any vehicle whose component parts (e.g. engine control unit, fuel injection/engine management software, electronic throttle) totally or partially fulfil the function of an SLD or ASLD falls under Part I, even without a discrete limiter device
Speed limiting implemented purely as an engine-management software function (SLF/ASLF) is covered, not only standalone hardware devices
A driver-settable speed limiter on any M or N vehicle, including M1 passenger cars and N1 vans, falls under the ASLD/ASLF provisions when fitted
Aftermarket or retrofit speed limiters can be approved as components under Part III and then installed under Part II
SLD approval relates to the fuel-feed control method; a change of control method creates a different SLD type
Vehicle type approval under Part I is bounded by the power/unladen mass ratio and the top-gear engine speed/vehicle speed ratio of the tested vehicle
Contracting Parties may require a plate in the driving compartment showing "SPEED LIMITER FITTED", the SLD calibrator and the set speed
Recommended for vehicles over 10 tonnes whose limitation speed is below the general speed limit
